basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment defines it; cardiac, GI and skeletal malformations are described as common (~30%+), without precise rates. Urogenital findings do not establish renal damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: structural GI and palatal anomalies are described as common, supporting approximately 30% or more; no precise frequency is available.

basis: Inherited susceptibility establishes future neuroblastoma risk, not an existing neural tumor or neurologic injury; no currently affected organ axis is established.

decisions.neurologic: none: susceptibility alone establishes future tumor risk; neither an existing neuroblastoma nor neurologic damage is established.

basis: Arterial disease, bone fragility and inherited cutis laxa define it; hydronephrosis 4/6. Seizures 2/6 omitted at cap; retinal tortuosity alone does not establish eye damage.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: inherited cutis laxa is an explicit parent and a structural skin manifestation of defective elastogenesis; cutis laxa occurs in 3/6.

basis: Split spinal cord and open hemicord myeloschisis define neural injury; the spina bifida aperta classification also establishes a vertebral closure defect.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: this open spinal dysraphism is a subtype of spina bifida aperta, with a defining vertebral closure defect as well as spinal cord malformation.

basis: Motor neuron degeneration defines ALS; muscle wasting and respiratory weakness reflect denervation, without evidence of intrinsic muscle or lung disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: weakness and muscle wasting are secondary to motor neuron loss and denervation; intrinsic muscle pathology is not the disease process.

basis: Cerebral arterial stenosis defines moyamoya; ischemic brain injury occurred in 2/2. Glaucoma in 1/2 is a separately diagnosed eye disease; hemianopia reflects brain injury.

decisions.neurologic: involved: arterial stenosis is the defining lesion; downstream ischemic stroke directly damages brain tissue and occurred in 2/2 patients.
decisions.ocular: none: glaucoma in 1/2 is a separate eye disease without established direct injury from moyamoya; hemianopia localizes to cerebral injury.

basis: Malignancy directly occupies cranial nerve VIII; lasting hearing loss from auditory nerve injury is common (>30%). Hearing function is explicitly included in the otologic axis.

decisions.otologic: involved: direct auditory nerve injury commonly causes persistent hearing loss (>30%); hearing is covered even without invasion of inner-ear structures.

basis: Defining renal, cardiac and palatal defects; lung hypoplasia 80-99%. Cap omits skeletal defects (polydactyly 80-99%) and callosal defects (30-79%), prioritizing severe organ dysfunction.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: defining cleft palate occurs in 80-99%; its feeding and oral functional burden warrants retention with the severe renal, cardiac and pulmonary defects.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none at cap: polydactyly occurs in 80-99% and other skeletal defects in 30-79%; the retained axes generally carry greater organ dysfunction.

basis: Complex I metabolic defect; leukodystrophy/developmental impairment and myopathy with ragged-red fibers reported in 1/1. Ocular motor signs alone do not establish intrinsic eye injury.

decisions.ocular: none: strabismus and nystagmus in 1/1 can reflect central motor dysfunction; no direct eye, retinal or optic nerve injury is established.

basis: Postviral immune-mediated granulomatous inflammation destroys thyroid follicles and disrupts hormone function; a proven active infection or autoimmune antibody is not required.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: subacute granulomatous thyroiditis involves immune-mediated follicular destruction, usually after a viral illness; the axis includes non-autoimmune immune-mediated disease.
